Let's parse structure: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to another phenyl ring bearing an α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2? Wait the amide is C(=O)N attached to phenyl (c3ccccc3N) meaning an aniline attached to carbonyl (amide) with NH attached to phenyl ring (anilide). So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl with an NH (aniline). So the amide is N-aryl (anilide) with an NH on the phenyl (i.e., an aniline substituent). So the target has three key bonds: sulfonamide N-S, amide C-N, and the C=C double bond formed via Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid). So retrosynthesis steps: 1) disconnect amide: break C(=O)-N bond to give carboxylic acid (α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). 2) disconnect the C=C double bond: break between the β carbon and α carbon to give aromatic aldehyde (p-tolyl-sulfonyl phenyl aldehyde?) Actually the α,β-unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl-sulfonyl phenyl (the aryl group). The double bond is between the phenyl ring (c2ccc) and the carbonyl side chain: /C=C/C(=O)N... So the β carbon is attached to phenyl ring (c2). So the precursor is an aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) attached to sulfonyl group. So step 2: Doebner modification: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid. So we need aldehyde precursor: c2ccc(C=O)cc2 with sulfonyl attached to N? Wait the sulfonamide attaches to the phenyl ring via N (the sulfonamide nitrogen attached to the first phenyl (p-tolyl) and sulfonyl attached to second phenyl (c2). So the sulfonyl group is attached to the second phenyl ring (c2). The sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the first phenyl (p-tolyl). So the aldehyde precursor would be the second phenyl bearing sulfonyl group attached to N? Actually the sulfonyl group is S(=O)(=O) attached to the second phenyl (c2) and also attached to the nitrogen of the first phenyl (p-tolyl). So the sulfonyl is bridging between the two phenyls via N-S bond. In retrosynthesis, we can disconnect sulfonamide formation: break N-S bond to give sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride) and aniline (p-tolyl amine). So step 3: sulfonamide formation from p-toluidine (p-methyl aniline) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (c2ccc(SO2Cl)cc2). That sulfonyl chloride can be derived from the same phenyl ring (c2) which also will be the aldehyde precursor. So overall route:

Target -> (retro amide) α,β-unsaturated acid + aniline (c3ccccc3N). The acid is: c2ccc(SO2NH-p-tolyl)CH=CHCOOH? Wait after breaking amide, we have acid: c2ccc(SO2NH-p-tolyl)CH=CHCOOH (the α,β-unsaturated acid). Then retro Doebner: break C=C to give aldehyde: c2ccc(SO2NH-p-tolyl)CHO and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). Then retro sulfonamide: break N-S to give p-toluidine (p-methyl aniline) and aryl sulfonyl chloride: c2ccc(SO2Cl)cc2 (the same phenyl ring). So three steps.
